title: Skyline Systems telemetry & resiliency workshop
summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing constraints, telemetry/observability integration for Redwood Private deployment, and resiliency patterns (failover, canary, regional fallback). Action items: share listing checklist, network diagram, and run a short flood test against staging deployment.
topics: KMS & key management for private deployments
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-09-09
- Start: 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~72 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ford (Redwood PM); Alex Rivera, Priya Desai, Omar Khalid, Jenny Park (Skyline)
- Recording link: https://redwood.share/example (placeholder)

Summary (auto): Short workshop to reconcile security/network requirements for Skyline's planned Private deployment and to specify telemetry ingestion and retention for marketplace listing.

--- Transcript body ---
[15:00] Maya Chen: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh i'm Maya from Redwood, i'll kick things off. can we do a quick round?
[15:02] Alex Rivera: Alex here, CTO at Skyline. excited to get this mapped out, we've got some tight windows for compliance.
[15:04] Priya Desai: Priya, lead SRE. main asks are: 1) how telemetry flows from Redwood Private to our observability stack, 2) cost/retention, and 3) isolation for PII sensitive traces.
[15:06] Ravi Patel: ravi here, i'll be the technical owner on the integration side. i can walk through the runtime telemetry hooks and where you can scrape metrics or ingest OTLP.
[15:07] Omar Khalid: omar, platform engineering. network and peering questions up front, we have a hub-and-spoke VPC architecture.
[15:09] Jenny Park: jenny from security, i'll be focused on keys and audit logs.

[15:10] Maya Chen: great. alex, can you summarize the desired deployment mode? you mentioned earlier you want private but also a marketplace listing. how are you picturing them?
[15:11] Alex Rivera: yes, we want a private managed control plane, with the inference nodes in our VPC — so kind of Redwood Private on-prem in cloud. marketplace listing is for our internal procurement, it needs an official listing and an approved ref arch doc. we also want the option to fall back to Redwood hosted if our region has capacity problems.
[15:13] Lena Ford: quick note — for marketplace listing we need a network topology diagram, KMS compatibility statement, and a short performance profile. we'll capture what gaps need docs.

[15:15] Ravi Patel: on telemetry: the runtime emits internal metrics via prometheus exposition and also supports OTLP/OTEL collector push. two common patterns: 1) allow Skyline to scrape Prom endpoints from within the VPC (we expose metrics on localhost or loopback with bind in sidecar), or 2) push OTLP via TLS to your ingest gateway. both are supported, but each has tradeoffs.
[15:17] Priya Desai: scraping is easier for us, we already have prometheus federation. question: does Redwood tag traces with model/version metadata and user-defined tenancy ids? we need to link traces to customer tenancy for audits.
[15:18] Ravi Patel: yes we add model/version, shard id, and tenant id if provided. small caveat — sometimes transcription of metadata names may change depending on the runtime plugin, but we can stabilize field names for the marketplace refarch.

[15:20] Omar Khalid: network question — if we expose a scrape endpoint, that requires peering or a private link. we prefer using a VPC endpoint that your agents push to, to avoid opening inbound. what does Redwood support for VPC connectivity?
[15:21] Maya Chen: we support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and static NAT egress with IP allow-listing. for on-prem we also support an outbound-only connector that tunnels to a customer-managed ingress.
[15:23] Jenny Park: for KMS: we need to bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and HSM-level assurances. can logs/audit trails be encrypted with keys we control?
[15:24] Ravi Patel: yes, for Private deployments you can integrate with your KMS; Redwood uses envelope encryption and can be configured to use CMKs. note: there are different UX flows for rotating keys — we'll document them for the refarch.

[15:26] Alex Rivera: can you also enumerate what gets into audit logs vs only short-lived telemetry? auditors will want user prompts, model version, api key id, and anomalies.
[15:27] Maya Chen: good point. out-of-the-box we capture request metadata for audit logs: request id, timestamp, model id, token counts, user id (if provided). PII content does not go into audit logs if you opt-in to filter — but we need to discuss retention windows.

[15:29] Priya Desai: retention: we want 90 days for traces and 1 year for audit events. what's feasible without exploding cost?
[15:30] Ravi Patel: retention is configurable; for high-cardinality traces the ingest cost is the big driver. we recommend sampling: 100% for errors + 1-5% baseline. that reduces cost while keeping error coverage.

[15:32] Omar Khalid: resiliency — if a zone goes down, can your runtime failover to a model in another region with minimal token loss? how does cache/KV behave across failover?
[15:33] Ravi Patel: currently KV cache is local per node to keep latency low; cross-region KV replication is possible but adds complexity. our recommended pattern is: 1) regional model variants with prefix cache warmers, 2) fast fallback to smaller model to sustain availability, and 3) multi-region canary with sticky routing. there is some cold-start cost when warming a new region.

[15:36] Alex Rivera: are there size / model constraints for the marketplace listing? we need to include quantization/throughput numbers in the listing doc.
[15:36] Lena Ford: we'll collect a short performance profile from you. our default is to include p50/p95 latencies at a standard prompt distribution and token rate. we can run a short benchmark on your staging to produce a one-page perf sheet.

[15:38] Priya Desai: security: SSO and RBAC for operators — we need SAML integration and fine-grained role mapping. can we map roles to specific deployment capabilities (scale, rollback, view-only)?
[15:39] Ravi Patel: yes SAML/SSO is supported for the control plane, and we expose RBAC roles that can be mapped to groups. mapping to specific ops actions is possible; we should draft a mapping matrix for the refarch.

[15:41] Jenny Park: also need tamper-evident audit logs and export to our SIEM (splunk). do you support streaming audit logs to an endpoint?
[15:42] Maya Chen: yes streaming to syslog/S3/Splunk via Kinesis is supported for Private. we can provide a lambda/collector example.

[15:44] Maya Chen: okay let me walk through a proposed network pattern on screen — (shared diagram link) — but verbally: hub VPC hosts shared services, spoke VPCs host workloads and our inference nodes in a private subnet, access via PrivateLink to control plane. metrics either pushed from sidecar to OTLP gateway (preferred) or scraped if you open a peering.

[15:46] Omar Khalid: (inaudible) — sorry, did you say sidecar or agent? we prefer a lightweight sidecar we control.
[15:47] Ravi Patel: sidecar — the sidecar runs the collector and can offload enrichment and batching. it also supports local sampling decisions. note: sidecar increases pod resources but gives more predictable telemetry.

[15:49] Alex Rivera: runbook question: during upgrades can we keep a canary and fallback? we require <2% error spike during canary. what are your rollback timings?
[15:50] Ravi Patel: typical canary windows 10-30 minutes depending on traffic; we support automatic rollback on error thresholds. rollout speed depends on model size and whether the cache is warm. we'll include recommended thresholds in the refarch.

[15:52] Priya Desai: testing — we want a flood test that simulates 200% normal token volume for 10 minutes on staging. will that damage the service?
[15:53] Maya Chen: we can coordinate a controlled flood on staging; we'll throttle if it threatens shared infra. recommended is to run the test against your dedicated staging capacity. we'll provide a test plan.

[15:55] Lena Ford: for the marketplace listing doc we'll need: short refarch (network + keys), perf profile (p50/p95), telemetry integration guide (prom/otlp examples), and security checklist (saml, kms, audit retention).

[15:57] Omar Khalid: data residency: some tenants will require EU-only storage. can we pin model inference and logs to region?
[15:58] Ravi Patel: yes we support region pinning for both runtime and logs. for cross-region replication we mark data categories and can restrict replication.

[16:00] Jenny Park: minor note — ensure the KMS key rotation flow doesn't break live connections. we've seen some vendors with a 2-hour outage during rotation.
[16:01] Ravi Patel: we have rolling key rotation that uses double-encryption during rotation, but we will include explicit runbook steps for your security team to validate.

[16:03] Alex Rivera: any competitor wonky behaviors we should watch for while we choose a vendor?
[16:03] Maya Chen: quick note — some vendors only support plaintext scrape endpoints which can cause compliance issues; others force all telemetry to hosted ingestion which breaks offline/on-prem needs. we'll highlight the differences in the doc.

[16:05] Priya Desai: do you have an agent for flamegraphs and slow traces for model execution? we need visibility into token generation time per-token.
[16:06] Ravi Patel: we export fine-grained latencies with per-token breakdown as an optional debug mode — that can be gated behind RBAC and sample only on failure to avoid cost.

[16:08] Maya Chen: okay, let's recap next steps and owners.
[16:09] Alex Rivera: sounds good.

[16:10] Maya Chen: recap: 1) we'll send a draft refarch and marketplace checklist, 2) we'll share a sample OTLP collector config and a prometheus scrape example, 3) schedule a short staging flood test, 4) produce a perf profile from a short benchmark.

[16:12] Omar Khalid: can we get the network diagram in editable form?
[16:13] Lena Ford: yes, we'll share a visio/diagrams.net link.

[16:15] Jenny Park: we'll send a security constraints doc for KMS/HSM requirements and retention windows.

[16:17] Maya Chen: great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the action items.

--- End transcript ---
